title: Choose the visual world
question: Bridge of Hope Foundation — keep the dealt direction, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Cooperative Ledger
options.lineage: cooperative account books, carbon triplicate forms, rubber-stamped receipts
options.thesis: The site is the foundation's books: every programme posted as a dated, numbered, stamped entry, impact read down the columns, and the funding ask ruled across the foot as the total.
options.viewport: A two-page ledger spread across the full viewport — programmes posted down the left, a stamped entry at the right, and one total row ruled across the foot carrying the 600 million XAF ask.
options.risk: Reads as dry bureaucracy if the stamp, rules and serial numbers are timid — paperwork only becomes proof when it is committed.

raised.raise: Partner and ACE-sibling logos are ranked as one deliberate sponsor strip along a single seam, never a scattered logo cloud.
Every figure wears its own stitched provenance label — source, date, and whether it is a target or a recorded actual.
Rehabilitation to skills to markets to dignity runs as one continuous downward flow through the page, not four separate cards.
Instrument-row restraint: one row of identical entries read by sweeping, and red used exactly once — on the funding gap.

regions.label: total row — the ask, ruled across the foot

options.label: The Joined Strip
options.lineage: Cameroonian Ndop narrow-loom cloth — strips woven alone, then sewn edge to edge
options.thesis: Each programme is woven as its own strip and joined edge to edge into one cloth; the site is the joining, and every seam stays visible.
options.viewport: Four vertical strips fill the first viewport — rehabilitation, skills, advocacy, livelihood — meeting under one bright seam that carries the ask.
options.risk: The expected move for a Cameroonian NGO, and it fails the moment the cloth becomes a background pattern instead of the layout itself.

regions.label: the seam — one cloth, the ask

options.label: The Brodovitch Spread
options.lineage: Harper's Bazaar under Brodovitch — didot hairlines choreographed across a two-page gutter
options.thesis: Each claim poses on the left page and its evidence answers on the right, the gutter holding the beat like a breath.
options.viewport: A photograph bleeding to the gutter on the left, a didot headline curving down the right, one lipstick-red live element.
options.case: Holds audience identification — international donors read photo-essay annual reports every day. Loses product clarity — the gutter choreography serves the story, not the Francophone family hunting for a service or the action they came to take.
options.risk: Reads as fashion editorial when the register outranks the offer.

options.label: The Napkin Zine
options.lineage: hand-drawn technical zines — marker lettering, doodle arrows, mascots
options.thesis: The model is taught the way a friend sketches it on a napkin: how rehabilitation becomes income, drawn panel by panel.
options.viewport: A hand-lettered headline above one doodled pathway diagram, arrows looping from intake to income, a highlighter swipe on the line that matters.
options.case: Holds product clarity — the doodle explains the four-pillar pathway better than any paragraph. Loses audience identification — marker-and-mascot playfulness undercuts the register a one-million-dollar institutional donor reads.
options.risk: Reads as a school newsletter if the drawing is not drafted with real precision.

options.label: The Vinyl Wrap
options.lineage: itasha vinyl wraps across car body panels
options.thesis: Programme art scaled so large it breaks across panels, partners ranged as sponsor strips along the sill.
options.viewport: Art breaking across a door seam with a ranked partner strip along the sill.
options.case: Fuses poorly: donors and families do not identify with pop-culture car culture.
options.kept: The sill — partners ranked as one deliberate strip along a single seam, never a logo cloud.

options.label: The Memory Quilt
options.lineage: hand-pieced quilts of worn garments and handwritten cloth
options.thesis: Each programme pieced from worn cloth with a label naming its body, date and domestic history.
options.viewport: Unequal patches under one line of bright new stitching.
options.case: Fuses poorly: quilting is a Western domestic tradition; the institutional record is the artifact this audience trusts.
options.kept: Every patch carries a body, a date and a provenance caption stitched to it — so every figure on the site wears its source.

options.label: The Glaze River
options.lineage: a kiln shelf beneath heavily glazed cups
options.thesis: Programmes flow down the page like molten glaze — pooling, arresting, and sometimes fusing into independence.
options.viewport: Cobalt running to the foot of a cup and freezing a millimetre above the shelf.
options.case: Fuses poorly: ceramics is a connoisseur's world; neither donor nor family identifies with it.
options.kept: One continuous flow as the page's spine — rehabilitation to skills to markets to dignity is a single downward path, not four cards.

options.label: The VU Bridge
options.lineage: a row of ballistic VU meters across a recording desk
options.thesis: Impact read as one row of identical needles, all leaning together on the same downbeat.
options.viewport: A row of identical meters swept left to right, red only past zero.
options.case: Fuses poorly: analog gear belongs to another audience, and needles would invent measurements the foundation does not yet have.
options.kept: Instrument-row restraint — one row of identical entries read by sweeping, and red used exactly once, on the funding gap.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What every NGO site ships: a hopeful hero photograph, three equal programme cards, a blue Donate button.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement a visitor expects, executed at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other NGO site, by design.
